title: Coarse resume checkpoint on the Uniboost staker deploy: a post-CREATE / pre-wiring abort makes resume permanently skip the five wiring txs, cementing a silently-unwired NFTStakerDepletion behind a 'verified' banner
description: _finalizeUniboost guards the entire NFTStakerDepletion deploy-plus-wire block as a single unit via `if (_isDeployed(stakerName)) return staker;` (line 472). `new NFTStakerDepletion(...)` lands and _trackDeployment sets deployed=true (line 482), which _writeProgressFile() PERSISTS (line 483) BEFORE any of the five wiring txs (setDispatcherHook / hook.setRecipient(staker) / setDepletionWindow / setPauser / Pauser.register, lines 487-491). If the non-atomic broadcast aborts after the CREATE tx but before all five wiring txs land, a resume sees deployed==true and returns early, permanently skipping the wiring. _verifyFinalState (621-641) asserts no staker-wiring invariant, so the run still reports success.
impact: A precisely-timed broadcast abort at the post-CREATE / pre-wiring boundary yields a deployed-but-unwired NFTStakerDepletion: dispatcherHook==0 (the staker cannot pull(), so accrued phUSD mint-debt is never realized to stakers), the Uniboost hook.recipient != staker (donations/debt mis-routed), depletionWindow==0, and the staker is unregistered with the global Pauser (no pause / break-glass coverage). Aggravator: _verifyFinalState asserts none of this, so the misconfiguration is SILENT and can persist in production until someone notices debt is not accruing. NO permanent loss: the accrued mint-debt stays parked in the hook ledger and is fully recoverable once an owner manually replays the five wiring txs and pull()s. This is the CEILING of Low: Medium was explicitly considered (it impairs a protocol feature's availability, and the silent success banner raises effective impact) and rejected because there is no value leak, the trigger is a low-likelihood operator-timing event on a controlled one-shot broadcast with no external-attacker surface, and recovery uses known in-script steps. Flagged so a triager can weigh the silent-availability aggravator deliberately (consistent with the run-19 deploy:ratchet-mainnet class-sibling, which was Low on the same non-atomic-resume logic; call re-derived here on its own facts, not inherited).
attackPath: Operator broadcasts the cutover (--slow --skip-simulation, one tx at a time).
`new NFTStakerDepletion(...)` (line 478) lands; _trackDeployment sets deployed=true (482) and _writeProgressFile() PERSISTS deployed=true (483) BEFORE any wiring.
The broadcast aborts after the CREATE tx but before all five wiring txs (487-491) land.
Operator re-runs to resume; `if (_isDeployed(stakerName)) return staker;` (472) sees deployed==true and RETURNS EARLY -> the five wiring txs are permanently skipped.
_verifyFinalState (621-641) asserts no staker-wiring invariant -> run reports success over a silently-unwired staker.
Recovery requires an owner to notice and manually replay setDispatcherHook / hook.setRecipient / setDepletionWindow / setPauser / Pauser.register, then pull().
recommendation: Checkpoint each wiring step individually (as Phases 1/2/4 do) or split the _isDeployed guard so the five wiring txs re-run on resume even when the CREATE already landed. Additionally, add the staker-wiring invariants to _verifyFinalState (staker.dispatcherHook == the deployed hook, hook.recipient == staker, depletionWindow != 0, Pauser.isRegistered(staker)) so a silent skip becomes a loud, caught revert rather than a 'verified' banner over a broken wiring.

mediumVsLow.verdict: Low (ceiling-of-Low; Medium explicitly considered and rejected).
mediumVsLow.caseForMedium: It impairs a protocol feature's function/availability (an unwired Uniboost staker: no debt realization, mis-routed donations, no pause coverage), and the SILENCE is a real aggravator because _verifyFinalState prints 'verified' over the broken state.
mediumVsLow.caseForLow: No loss (mint-debt parked in the hook ledger, fully owner-recoverable); a precisely-timed abort of a controlled one-shot broadcast with no external-attacker surface; owner-fixable with known in-script steps.
mediumVsLow.decisiveReasoning: Full recoverability + no value leaving the system + a low-likelihood operator-timing trigger + no external-attacker surface outweigh the (real) silent-availability aggravator. The aggravator is a reason to fix BOTH this and UBC-03, not to relabel a recoverable, no-loss, precisely-timed footgun as Medium.
